chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Durays ibn A'yan, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who set out performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj) for the Hajj, but did not reach Mecca except on the Day of Sacrifice. He said: He remains in his state of Ihram, and cuts off the Talbiyah when he enters Mecca, and performs Tawaf and Sa'i between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and shaves his head, and returns to his family if he wishes.
And he said: This is for the one who made a condition upon his Lord at the time of his Ihram. If he did not make the condition, then upon him is the Hajj of the following year.

key_terms.إِحْرَامِهِ: Ihram (the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.اشْتَرَطَ: Conditioned (referring to the condition of 'If Hajj prevents me, then I am released from it, making it Umrah')
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةَ: Talbiyah (the recitation of 'Labbayk Allahumma Labbayk' during Hajj/Umrah)
key_terms.السَّعْيُ: Sa'i (walking between the hills of Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.الْحَلْقُ: Halq (shaving the head, a rite of completion for Umrah or Hajj)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعًا: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj, with a break in Ihram)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who arrives in Mecca late and only has time to perform Umrah?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Baqir (AS) in *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the distinction between a conditional and unconditional pilgrim arriving late on the Day of Sacrifice, emphasizing that the condition (*shart*) at the onset of Ihram determines whether one exits Hajj status after Umrah or remains bound to complete the full Hajj rites. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the intention and stipulation at the start of the ritual dictate the legal outcome of delayed arrival. The text underscores the importance of precise intention (*niyyah*) in shaping the validity and completeness of the pilgrimage.
